text: hey everybody there's not a single syllable of the Bible that uses the phrase the word of God as a reference to the scriptures much less to the Bible
itself the Bible would not exist until centuries after the scriptures were all written and their authors were all dead
so in that sense the Bible is a post-biblical concept but when we find the phrase word of God in the Bible it's
sometimes being used to refer to Jesus in the New Testament but in many places in the New Testament and throughout the entire Hebrew Bible it is a reference to
the messages being communicated directly between God and humanity and these messages were conceptualized as distinct
from their written form as well as the stories about the people who are receiving and talking about those
messages so when we look at the Bible we have stories about people receiving Communications from God and sharing them
with others and we even have the written form of some of those messages but those are both distinct from what
was understood to be the word of God itself and even in the earliest generations of Christianity the words of
Jesus were considered distinct from the graffiti the written things because they were living words that were being
transmitted orally they were not frozen in text so the words of Jesus were superior to the Jewish scriptures and it
was not until we got a couple Generations away from Jesus's life when we no longer really had a plausible case to make for having heard the very words
of Jesus either first or second hand that they needed to be committed to text they needed to be preserved in their
written form and then we have the development of the gospels and the texts of the New Testament apart from the
letters of Paul and they begin to take on significance as graphy as scriptures as the written things but when you see
the word of God in the Bible this this is never a reference to the Bible or to the scriptures this is a reference to
the messages directly between God and Humanity or in the New Testament to Jesus himself
